why:
CORRECTED 2026-09-04 (phase-417 stage 6): this carried `provides: ["rclrs::log_trace"]`, and **`rclrs::log_trace` does not exist** -- rclrs's severity family stops at `debug`. The arrow was generated mechanically as `rclrs::log_<severity>` from the macro name during the throttle re-verdict, without checking the target resolves. That is the exact failure the `provides` authoring pass avoided by hand-writing every arrow, where two independent agents rejected ~76% of mechanically proposed candidates.

There is no upstream counterpart at TRACE, so this is an `extension`, not a re-map. See `rust:nros_trace`: rclrs has five severities and we have six.

phase-417 W4.d — a RE-MAP, not an addition. rclrs expresses throttling as a PARAMETER on one macro -- `log_info!(logger, throttle = Duration, "..")` via `LogParams`/`ToLogParams` -- where we ship a separate macro per severity. Same capability, decomposed differently: a parameter list needs named arguments the macro would have to parse off an arbitrary prefix, and a distinct name is what makes the throttled path resolvable at expansion.

The clock-reading form; without `nros-log/platform-clock` it is a `compile_error!` rather than a throttle that silently admits everything, and `*_throttle_at` takes the caller's timestamp instead.
